_0.11.0 was built and used locally but never tagged; this is the first tagged release of the series._

## Added

- `dossier` reads **who vouches for each page**: `pages[].trust` and
  `groups[].trust` are `official` for the Cadastre Committee's own documents
  (the ownership certificate, the reference letter and its fee table, the
  map extracts — recognised by their fixed labels and, for an extract whose
  heading is unreadable, by a turning-point table or several parcel codes
  with no sheet designation or drawing title), `applicant` for the form, the
  drawings and the notes, `identity` for a person's papers, `unknown` for a
  page nothing has read yet.
- `dossier` **`facts[]`**: every figure the dossier states about its parcel
  — cadastral codes, the parcel's area, registered buildings' areas, the
  fence's planned area, the owner, the applicant, the address, the
  certificate number, the turning-point tables' areas and perimeters — one
  entry per page that states it, with the page's trust. Read
  deterministically off the certificate's fixed labels, the form's
  «Նախատեսում եմ» line, the reference letter's «Դիմող», and context words
  on the same line before a printed area elsewhere. Legacy 8-bit Armenian
  fonts are decoded for this reading (`crates/pdf-dossier/src/legacy.rs`).
- `dossier` **`checks[]`**: each repeated figure compared across the pages
  that state it, the official page as the reference — `agree`,
  `near_miss`, `disagree`, `single_source`, or `unreadable` when the pages
  that would settle it are still owed to the vision pass. A mismatch names
  both pages and both values and is never resolved by picking a side. On the
  corpus this surfaces a fence stated as 3.0 m² on the form and 5.20 m² in
  the note, title blocks carrying another project's parcel code, a map
  requested by someone other than the registered owner, a joint extract
  covering two parcels, and a survey polygon 1.1 m² off the certificate.
- The vision answer may carry **`facts[]`** for a scanned page (kinds as
  above, `unit` `ha` \| `m2` for areas); `--vlm` asks for them and merges
  them with `via: "vlm"`.
- `docs/json-api.md`, *`facts` and `checks`*; `docs/annotation-schema.md`
  0.3.0.
- **The extraction scorecard** (`crates/pdf-toolkit/tests/scorecard.rs`):
  every kind of reading graded against a per-document ledger of what is on
  the page (`data/expected/`, seeded by `scripts/seed-expected.py`) and
  ratcheted against a committed baseline, so a change shows as "facts 0.99
  → 1.00, entities unchanged" per document rather than as a golden diff.

- `model --answers a.json`: the dossier's page labels name the floor plans,
  the roof plan and the elevations for a set whose title blocks the
  classifier cannot read; with three detection fallbacks — storey and roof
  levels from the elevations' level marks, a storey aligned on its drawing's
  centre when there are no grid labels (`origin_source: "fill_centre"`), a
  building box derived from the walls and rooms when no envelope fill is
  drawn — every corpus set now reaches the reconstruction, and the hosted
  `--llm-params` proposal is the way to settle the parameters where the
  fallbacks are approximate. `Reconstruction.warnings` carries what the
  rules worked around; a roof sheet that cannot be read omits the roof
  rather than the model.
- The scorecard's `building` kind grades the recorded hosted reconstruction
  (`data/annotations/building/<n>.json`) — parts, heights to 0.3 m,
  footprints to ten percent, placement — and its `model` kind runs from the
  recorded, accepted parameters (`data/annotations/model/<n>.params.json`)
  where a reviewed `--llm-params` run kept some.

## Fixed

- `structured` no longer panics on a page whose text runs right to left
  (a span of negative width put its coverage bins in reverse order).

## Changed

- Annotation schema 0.3.0 (additive: `trust`, `facts`, `checks`); workspace
  version 0.11.0. The reviewed annotations were regenerated; the only
  differences are the new fields.
